mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of quarters when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -3% AND HOUST < previous year's value * 0.9
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of instances meeting the dual GDPC1/HOUST trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 5-day forward returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day forward returns in more than 55% of months when INDPRO falls by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 2% over three months signals a precautionary savings behavior that foreshadows lower future demand and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous quarter + 5% AND GDPC1 < previous quarter * 0.98 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day forward returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) cut of at least 0.75 percentage points within a single quarter signals an aggressive easing cycle, which lowers long-term yields and boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of quarters following a 0.75%+ FEDFUNDS cut.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% and a fall in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month signals a deepening labor market downturn, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day forward returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals a secular demand shortfall, which erodes earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day forward returns in more than 55% of quarters when GDPC1 growth is below 1% for three consecutive quarters.
